jobs.title: Recruitment Resourcer
jobs.description:
About Chapter 2

At Chapter 2, we are redefining the future of talent through AI-powered and human-led solutions.

We combine technology with deep recruitment expertise to help ambitious organisations hire smarter, move faster and build teams that drive growth.

We don't operate like a traditional recruitment agency. Our Talent Partners work embedded within our clients' businesses, becoming a true extension of their teams and taking ownership of the hiring that matters.

As we continue to grow across Germany and mainland Europe, we're looking for talented recruiters and talent professionals who want to work differently.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Recruitment Resourcer / Talent Sourcer to join our Talent Operations team in Munich.

This role is ideal for someone who loves the search side of recruitment finding great people, understanding talent markets and building high-quality pipelines that enable recruiters and Talent Partners to deliver exceptional hiring outcomes.

You'll work closely with our Talent Partners and clients across a range of functions, with a particular focus on Technology, Product, Engineering and other specialist roles.

You don't need to come exclusively from tech recruitment, but we're particularly interested in people who have experience sourcing within the technology/start-up/scale-up ecosystem and understand how to identify hard-to-find talent.

This is a hands-on sourcing role where you'll have the opportunity to use LinkedIn Recruiter, AI and modern sourcing technology to work smarter and build better talent pipelines.

What You'll Do

• Partner with Talent Partners to understand hiring requirements and translate briefs into effective sourcing strategies.
• Build targeted talent pipelines across Technology, Engineering, Product, GTM and other specialist functions.
• Source candidates proactively using LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search, talent platforms, networks and creative sourcing techniques.
• Identify and engage passive candidates who may not be actively looking but could be a strong fit.
• Conduct initial candidate conversations and qualification screens where appropriate.
• Research talent markets, companies and competitor organisations to identify relevant talent pools.
• Maintain accurate candidate and pipeline data within our recruitment systems.
• Use recruitment data and market insights to continuously improve sourcing strategies.
• Leverage AI and recruitment technology to automate repetitive tasks, improve search quality and increase sourcing efficiency.
• Work closely with Talent Partners to ensure smooth handover and progression of qualified candidates.
• Support multiple searches and priorities across a fast-moving portfolio of clients.
• Represent Chapter 2 and our clients professionally in the German talent market.

What You'll Bring

• 3 –5+ years of recruitment sourcing/resourcing experience, ideally within tech, start-ups, scale-ups, agency, RPO, embedded or in-house recruitment.
• Fluent German and strong English communication skills.
• Experience sourcing candidates within the German market.
• Strong LinkedIn Recruiter and Boolean search skills.
• A genuine interest in technology, recruitment technology and the evolving world of AI.
• The ability to understand a recruitment brief and turn it into a targeted sourcing strategy.
• Strong research skills and a naturally curious approach to finding talent.
• Confidence engaging with passive candidates and building relationships from the first interaction.
• Excellent organisation skills and attention to detail.
• The ability to manage multiple searches and priorities without losing quality.
• A collaborative mindset and the ability to work closely with recruiters, Talent Partners and hiring managers.
• A proactive attitude, you're someone who enjoys figuring things out rather than waiting to be told what to do.

What Makes Chapter 2 Different?

You won't just be searching databases.

You'll be expected to understand the market, think creatively about where talent sits and build sourcing strategies that actually work.

You won't be measured by the number of CVs you send.

Quality matters. We're interested in finding the right people, not generating volume.

You'll work alongside experienced Talent Partners.

You'll become an important part of the delivery team, partnering closely with recruiters and gaining exposure to the full recruitment lifecycle.

AI is part of how we work.

We're building a modern recruitment function where AI and technology enhance human expertise — helping us research faster, search smarter and spend more time doing the work that genuinely requires a human touch.

You'll work with interesting companies.

Our clients include ambitious, high-growth organisations across Germany and Europe, giving you exposure to different industries, talent markets and challenging searches.

What We Offer

• Hybrid working from Munich.
• The opportunity to work with ambitious, high-growth companies across Germany and Europe.
• An embedded recruitment model rather than transactional agency recruitment.
• Exposure to Technology, Product, GTM and other specialist talent markets.
• A modern, AI-enabled approach to sourcing and recruitment.
• Real ownership and the opportunity to develop your recruitment career.
• Dedicated time and budget for learning and development.
• A collaborative Talent Operations team with coaching, knowledge sharing and support.
• The opportunity to grow with a scaling Talent Operations business.
• The chance to help shape how modern recruitment is done at Chapter 2.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Thermo Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.location: Reno, Nevada, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

Role Summary

Amperesand is looking for a Senior Staff Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer to play a key technical leadership role in developing its next-generation medium-voltage solid-state power conversion platform. This is a highly hands-on, end-to-end role where you’ll own the architecture of our complete thermal system—from architecture and concept selection, system sizing and modeling, CAD and detailed design, thermal CFD simulation, coolant and airflow routing, design for manufacturing and assembly, thermal system validation, and troubleshooting.

You’ll work closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, quality, suppliers, and factory teams to design, develop, and build the best system for a novel application, solve problems that don’t have established answers, with the opportunity to own thermal design.  Thermal performance is key to the overall performance of our solid-state power converter and a key differentiator for Amperesand.  We are looking for someone with deep thermal system design expertise, system modeling, detailed design experience, and a track record of independently leading complex technical work and solving novel problems.  We are not looking for someone who simply executes to a defined specification. The role can be based in Reno, San Francisco, or the South Bay.

What You’ll Do

• Own the complete thermal system for Amperesand’s solid-state power conversion platform from architecture into mass-production.

• Select the architecture of our next-generation thermal system to meet and exceed product-level requirements.

• Concept selection for how to implement the selected architecture.

• Model the thermal system performance across our operating conditions and mission profiles.

• Detailed design of the thermal system components, including CAD, and thermal CFD.

• Partner with the manufacturing and quality teams on DFM/DFA activities to ensure the thermal system design is manufacturable.

• Prototyping and validation of the thermal system.

• Problem solving anywhere and everywhere between architecture and start of production.

What You’ll Bring

• Master’s or PhD in mechanical engineering or related field, BS with evidence of exceptional accomplishment

• Thermal system design, mechanical design, CAE expertise

• Demonstrated ability to deliver a thermal system and solve novel engineering problems

• Hands-on testing and validation experience

• Ability for technical leadership of 1-3 junior engineers working under you on the thermal system

Nice to Have

jobs.title: Senior Material Planning Program Manager, Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

Amperesand is building next-generation power infrastructure systems for Data Centers, EV charging platforms, and future energy applications. Our systems combine advanced power electronics, embedded controls, and scalable energy architectures to rethink how power is converted, controlled, and deployed.

About the Role

Every SST we ship depends on hundreds of components arriving on time, in the right quantities - across a supply base that's ramping as fast as our product roadmap. This role sits inside our Supply Chain organization and owns the planning discipline that keeps that possible: translating engineering schedules and customer demand signals into a material plan the whole company can build against.

What You’ll do

Material Planning & Execution

• Own end-to-end material planning across our BOMs - demand/supply reconciliation, buffer and safety-stock strategy, and purchase prioritization that keeps pace with engineering change

• Translate program schedules into concrete, current material plans; know at any given moment what's on track, what's at risk, and what needs to move

• Continuously monitor supplier lead times, MOQs, allocation, and other risk

Supply Readiness & Risk

• Partner with GSMs and SIEs to close gaps before they threaten a build

• Track program-level clear-to-build status and drive the cross-functional work to unblock it before it becomes a hard stop

• Own the material and inventory impact of supply impacting ECOs from assessment through implementation - quantifying exposure, and keeping the program informed of what's changing and why it matters

Systems & Scale

• Work with software team to build the planning tools, dashboards, and processes - spanning PLM, ERP, and MRP - that give Supply Chain, Engineering, and Manufacturing one shared, trustworthy view of material readiness

• Design for the business we're scaling, not just the build in front of us.

What You’ll bring

• 5-8+ years in material planning, program management, or supply chain roles supporting complex hardware, with hands-on ownership of large, multi-hundred-line BOMs from development through ramp

• Strong working knowledge of demand/supply planning, supplier readiness, and the cost/material impact of quality and engineering changes

• Experience standing up planning or supply-readiness processes from scratch - not just operating inside systems someone else built

• A track record of spotting problems weeks before they land, and driving resolution across engineering, sourcing, and manufacturing teams

• Comfort with ambiguity and a genuine interest in shaping how a fast-growing hardware company plans and scales

• BS in Supply Chain, Data Analytics, or a related field

Please note: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options.

Onsite Collaboration Rationale:
Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.

Why Join Amperesand

• Work on next-generation power infrastructure systems • High ownership and visibility • Cross-functional collaboration • Opportunity to shape future products and infrastructure • Fast-moving startup environment

jobs.title: Miner
jobs.description:
As Miner your responsibilities will include but not limited to:

Safety, Health, and Environment:

• Adhere to all health and safety practices and requirements.
• Maintain good housekeeping to ensure compliance and an environment where team members can deliver their outputs within a controlled risk environment.
• Active participation in VFL’s, relevant Risk Assessments an close-out of Safety Actions

Floor Stock:

• Exercise the necessary control over activities that do not adversely affect the environment and the immediate community. For example, ensure the right amount of charge to minimise vibrations and the impact of blasting on the community (especially fly-rock).
• Measure drilled holes (primary and secondary blasting) according to the plan to determine the accurate quantity of explosives and accessories.
• Obtain the precise amount of blasting accessories from the explosive magazine.
• Charge blasting holes with the prescribed explosives to ensure the required fragmentation.
• Inspect the blasting area after the blasting operation for misfires and unsafe conditions and declare it safe for normal operations.
• Destroy all surplus and damaged explosives after each blasting operation according to the Mine Health & Safety Act.
• Compile the Blasting report and forward it to the supervisor within the agreed-upon time.
• Exercising control over explosives.

Controlled team activities:

• Observe and enforce any codes of practice, instructions, procedures, directives, permissions, exemptions, etc., issued by the mine, the Department of Mineral Resources or any other person authorised.
• Deliver outputs within the agreed timeframes and add value to the business.
• Deploy subordinates (direct and indirect) effectively and plan their tasks proactively to ensure smooth production operation.
• Perform effective and efficient general office administration, such as diary management and order processing, thus contributing to achieving the team's objectives.
• Create SAP orders and follow-up.
• Take minutes in sectional meetings.

Clean and environmentally friendly work area:

• Keep the environment clean.
• Perform cleaning activities beyond the allocated area.
• Clean equipment with the appropriate tools.
• Maintain good housekeeping standards.
• Ensure all blasting activities follow legislation and required processes and procedures.

Assistance:

• Assist the supervisor and co-workers according to their level/area of competence and follow company policies when instructed or during the responsible person's absence to ensure the achievement of functional objectives.
• Assist the supervisor actively in continuous improvement projects.

This role is in Mining (MIN) on a Band 6 (C-Lower) level reporting to the Blasting Supervisor/Shift Supervisor.

• Grade 12/N3 Technical
• Opencast Blasting Certificate
• Valid Kumba Dover Certificate
• Legal Liability certificate is preferred
• Hazchem is preferred
• Competency A is preferred
• SA Drivers Licence: Code B (Light Vehicle)

Technical Knowledge

• 3-5 years of previous mining blasting operational experience.
• Knowledge of mining blasting processes.
• Knowledge of the Mine, Health and Safety Act and Regulations.
• Knowledge of the Explosives Act & Regulations.

Who we are?

Anglo American is a global diversified mining business. Our portfolio of world-class mining operations provides the metals and minerals that make modern life possible. We use innovative practices and the latest technologies to discover new resources and mine.

We work together with our key partners and stakeholders to unlock the sustainable value that those resources represent for our shareholders, the communities and countries in which we operate and for society at large. Anglo American is re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.

How we are committed to your safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How to apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

jobs.title: Internal Control, Audit & Process Specialist
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing hands-on experience in internal control and audit remediation and at the same time gaining regional exposure and working closely with senior management? Then this role, which is based in Madrid is an attractive opportunity.

Position Objective

• Provide regional governance, coordination, and technical guidance to EMEA entities on internal control (SICS) and Corporate Internal Audit–related topics.
• The role supports countries before the Corporate Internal Audits and controls the follow-up and closure of audit findings, ensuring consistent improvements in both, internal audit performance and remediation of findings.
• The role supports countries before the Corporate Internal Audits and controls the follow-up and closure of audit findings, ensuring timely, effective, and sustainable remediation and continuous improvement of the internal audit readiness across EMEA.
• This role does not perform internal audits, does not participate in audit fieldwork, and does not interact with external auditors.

Main Responsibilities / Key Accountabilities

1. Internal Control & SICS Governance

• Act as the EMEA reference for internal control (SICS) and audit-related governance topics.
• Drive consistent understanding and application of SICS requirements across EMEA entities through hands-on guidance and review of implementation quality.
• Translate Corporate governance expectations into pragmatic regional guidance, considering scale and complexity of the region, and actively review whether controls are designed and operating as intended.

2. Audit Readiness & Preventive Support

• Analyze recurrent findings and common weaknesses identified in Corporate Internal Audits.
• Proactively support countries scheduled for upcoming Corporate Internal Audits through preparation guidance and clarification of expectations.
• Strengthen audit readiness without replacing, diluting, or taking over local management accountability.

3. Follow-up and Closure of Audit Findings (Critical Responsibility)

• Own regional tracking, monitoring, and escalation of findings resulting from Corporate Internal Audits.
• Ensure action plans are clearly defined, responsibilities assigned (GM-owned), deadlines respected, and remediation evidence properly documented.
• Ensure audit findings are closed in substance, not only formally closed in systems.
• Escalate overdue or critical findings to Area and Regional management as required.

4. Governance Frameworks & Policies

• Establish and maintain regional governance frameworks for selected topics (e.g. Manual of Authority – MoA), with a focus on practical application and effectiveness.
• Ensure alignment between Corporate requirements, regional standards, and local implementation.

5. Process Improvement & Best Practices

• Identify structural control or process weaknesses observed across multiple countries.
• Propose pragmatic improvements and share best practices across EMEA, avoiding unnecessary complexity and bureaucracy.

Authority & Decision Rights

• No authority to perform, influence, or interfere with Corporate Internal Audits.
• No involvement during internal audit execution or fieldwork.
• Authority to define regional governance standards within Corporate frameworks.
• Authority to challenge and escalate issues related to internal control, SICS implementation, and audit findings.

Key Stakeholders

• Local Finance Managers and Controllers
• Country and Area General Managers
• Area / Regional Finance Leadership
• Corporate Internal Audit
• Corporate SICS teams

Scope & Complexity

• EMEA region with ~65 countries and highly diverse regulatory environments.
• Strong coordination and governance role with limited operational depth per country.
• Impact-based prioritization is required to ensure scalability and effectiveness.
• No direct reports.

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Audit, or a related field is a must
• Fluent English, both written and verbal; additional languages - especially Spanish - are an advantage in a diverse EMEA environment
• Proven experience and minimum 5 years in internal control, governance, audit readiness, risk management, or a comparable corporate assurance function
• Solid understanding of internal control frameworks (e.g., SICS or similar) and how to assess control design and operational effectiveness
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively and collaborate across countries and seniorities
• Highly structured, organized, and detail‑oriented, with the ability to manage complex follow-up processes and monitor multiple audit findings simultaneously
• Strong analytical mindset, able to spot patterns, identify structural weaknesses, and translate them into practical, scalable improvements
• A proactive, solutions-oriented working style, comfortable balancing governance expectations with pragmatic business realities in a multinational context

• We offer intensive training and interesting perspectives for anyone who wants to build a career
• Sika is like a global SME: With subsidiaries in more than 100 countries around the world. This begins in Switzerland and breaks down borders allowing exciting prospects all around the world
• The chance to bring new ideas, interesting areas for development, and taking responsibility early on are some of the key factors that drive Sika's pioneering spirit

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager, Advertising
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure the responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. In support of that mission, the Marketing team helps deeply understand customer audiences and market dynamics, influence the development of the right products, build sustainable and customer-aligned monetization models, and drive awareness, adoption, and usage across OpenAI’s products and platform.

We take a data-driven approach to understand markets, develop monetization strategies, and uncover customer needs that shape product strategy and messaging. We partner closely with Sales, Partnerships, Product, Engineering, Research, Comms, and Design to deliver a cohesive end-to-end customer experience and lead go-to-market efforts for new product launches across channels.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Advertising to bring together advertiser insights, market understanding, and product knowledge to shape positioning, inform product priorities, and deliver go-to-market initiatives that drive adoption and measurable business impact.

You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Partnerships to understand advertiser needs, translate complex AI capabilities into clear customer value, and bring new products and features to market. This role is ideal for someone who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, independently navigates ambiguity, and brings cross-functional partners together to deliver results.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL:

 - Define the product and marketing strategy for a component of OpenAI’s advertising business in partnership with cross-functional partners

 - Develop a deep understanding of advertisers through customer research, market analysis, and competitive insights, identifying opportunities to improve positioning, adoption, and product-market fit.

 - Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating complex capabilities into compelling narratives for different advertiser audiences and use cases.

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to bring advertiser needs and market insights into roadmap discussions and product decisions.

 - Develop and drive go-to-market plans for new products and features, owning marketing execution from planning through launch and ongoing adoption.

 - Create advertiser-facing content and sales enablement materials, including product narratives, sales decks, one-pagers, FAQs, and launch communications.

 - Partner with Sales, Partnerships, Data Science, and Analytics to define success metrics, assess launch and adoption performance, and turn findings into improvements.

 - Surface advertiser concerns and launch risks related to performance, safety, policy, and trust, working with the relevant teams to address them in launch plans and customer communications.

 - Align cross-functional partners around priorities, responsibilities, and timelines, making thoughtful tradeoffs and resolving blockers within your initiatives.

 - Build repeatable approaches to launches, messaging, and enablement, sharing learnings and mentoring peers to improve the team’s storytelling and execution.




YOU MIGHT BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU…

 - Have experience independently developing product and marketing strategies and bringing products to market, particularly in advertising, marketing technology, platforms, or data and AI.

 - Have experience in structured problem solving environments including but not limited to strategy/management consulting, investment banking, corporate strategy and venture capital

 - Understand advertiser goals and the advertising ecosystem, including measurement, targeting and relevance, creative, auctions, and performance tradeoffs.

 - Communicate clearly and persuasively, translating technical concepts into differentiated customer value for a range of audiences.

 - Use qualitative and quantitative evidence—including customer interviews, surveys, adoption data, and experiments—to make decisions and improve results.

 - Bring structured problem solving and strong judgment to ambiguous challenges, independently setting priorities and managing initiatives from strategy through execution.

 - Build effective partnerships across Product, Engineering, Sales, and other teams, influencing decisions and driving alignment without formal authority.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
ABOUT FOCUSED ENERGY

Focused Energy is a pioneering international deep-tech company with locations in Germany and the US, dedicated to commercializing laser-driven nuclear fusion. Our mission is to deliver clean, safe, and virtually limitless energy to the world. As we rapidly scale, we seek talented individuals who thrive on bringing clarity and structure to fast-growing environments.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will be the primary software point of contact for the Laser team and provide technical leadership across software, hardware, and experimental-system interfaces. You will help define the architecture and technology direction for a greenfield laser-software platform while remaining hands-on in developing reliable tools for calibration, operation, human-machine interaction, and experimental data processing.

This role offers the opportunity to work across software, hardware, and experimental-system boundaries while contributing to a strong engineering culture within the Darmstadt Software Department. You will help shape technical direction, establish the foundations of a new software platform, and grow toward a broader technical leadership role. The position does not initially include direct people-management responsibility.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Act as the primary software partner for the Laser team and coordinate software activities across laser projects.

 - Provide technical leadership for software initiatives, including planning, technical alignment, risk identification, and coordination with laser physicists, engineers, and systems-integration partners.

 - Help define the architecture, technology choices, development practices, and interfaces for a new laser-software platform in a greenfield environment.

 - Design and implement reliable software for critical laser projects, from system-level interfaces to user-facing applications.

 - Develop and maintain automated calibration software that improves repeatability, reduces manual effort, and supports reliable laser operation.

 - Design and build clear, dependable human-machine interfaces, dashboards, and operational tools for monitoring and operating laser systems.

 - Develop software that interfaces with laser devices, diagnostic systems, cameras, and experimental equipment to support data acquisition, system monitoring, operational control, and visualization.

 - Develop data-processing pipelines and data-storage solutions for experimental and operational data, including diagnostic and camera data where appropriate.

 - Define robust interfaces between software, hardware, cameras, and experimental systems in an environment where requirements and technologies are still evolving.

 - Work with networked device and system interfaces, potentially including TCP/IP, REST APIs, webhooks, DDS, SCADA, or comparable communication technologies.

 - Write automated tests, technical documentation, and operational guidance to support long-term maintainability and safe, reliable operation.

 - Identify and address reliability, performance, integration, debugging, and maintenance risks in software that interacts with real-world systems.

 - Contribute to technical design discussions, code reviews, and knowledge sharing across the Software Department.

 - Mentor engineers and help establish engineering practices as the software team grows.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You are an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving complex, ambiguous technical problems and building systems from the ground up.

 - You are comfortable taking ownership of technical direction while collaborating closely with software specialists, laser physicists, experimental experts, and systems-integration partners.

 - You can move effectively between technical leadership, project coordination, architecture, and hands-on implementation.

 - You take ownership of the quality, reliability, testability, and long-term maintainability of the systems you build.

 - You communicate clearly with both software specialists and technical partners from adjacent disciplines.

 - You apply sound technical judgment when making design, implementation, and technology-selection decisions in an evolving environment.

 - You are curious, adaptable, and motivated to understand how software interacts with hardware, cameras, diagnostics, and experimental systems.

 - You are experienced in debugging and testing complex software and understand their importance in senior-level engineering work.

 - You value constructive feedback, knowledge sharing, and mentoring other engineers.

 - You are interested in developing toward technical leadership and project ownership. Formal people-management responsibility is not required at the outset.


DESIRABLE SKILLS & KNOWLEDGE

 - Strong programming experience in C++, Python, or comparable programming languages.

 - Experience designing, implementing, testing, debugging, and maintaining complex software systems.

 - Knowledge of software architecture, code review practices, automated testing, technical documentation, and engineering best practices.

 - Experience with greenfield development, platform or architecture definition, and making technology choices where requirements are still evolving.

 - Experience with automated calibration, control-adjacent software, laboratory systems, automation, or physical-device interfaces.

 - Experience developing human-machine interfaces, dashboards, or software for operating technical equipment.

 - Experience with camera integration, image processing, diagnostic data, or experimental data-processing pipelines.

 - Experience developing data-storage solutions for high-volume, time-series, experimental, or operational data.

 - Familiarity with software-hardware integration and working across experimental-system boundaries.

 - Experience with networked device communication or system interfaces, such as TCP/IP, REST APIs, webhooks, DDS, SCADA, or comparable technologies.

 - Familiarity with control systems or optics is beneficial, but not required; the ability to learn and collaborate across these disciplines is more important.

 - Previous experience mentoring engineers or leading technical design discussions.


Focused Energy is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Focused Energy will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, benefits.

• Monitor, report, and drive performance against service level agreements (SLAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs).

• Ensure partners adhere to established operational processes and compliance requirements.

• Serve as the voice of the partner within Rocket Travel by Agoda, advocating for their needs and ensuring alignment with internal teams.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work closely with Operations, Enablement, Project, Commercial, and Support teams to deliver on partner requirements and drive continuous improvement.

• Facilitate regular communication and alignment between partners and internal stakeholders to ensure program objectives are met.

Partner Relationship Management

• Understand partners’ business goals, operational challenges, and customer service expectations.

• Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to partners to optimize service delivery and customer experience.

• Prepare and deliver regular performance updates to partners and internal stakeholders.

• Gather and act on feedback from partners to drive operational improvements and enhance the customer journey.

• Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills, with a collaborative and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Excellent organizational and project management abilities; able to manage multiple priorities and deliver results.

• Analytical and data-driven, with the ability to synthesize information and make strategic recommendations.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to present to and influence senior stakeholders.

• Comfortable working in a hybrid, multicultural, and matrixed environment.

Candidates should be authorized to accept employment in the US from any employer and must be able to work a hybrid work schedule with 2-3 days per week in the stated physical office (unless otherwise indicated).

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer - Platform
jobs.description:
Ebury helps ambitious businesses unlock global growth, and we take the same approach with our people. We encourage innovation and movement, collaboration and problem-solving, and foster an environment where everyone can feel they belong, are valued, supported and empowered to succeed.

If you’re a collaborator who wants to help transform how businesses operate globally, get in touch - we’d love to discuss how Ebury can accelerate your career so you can shape the future.

Senior Data Engineer - Platform

Madrid Office - Hybrid: 4 days in the office, 1 day working from home

Join Our Data Team at Ebury Valencia office.

Ebury's strategic growth plan would not be possible without our Data team and we are seeking a Senior Data Engineer to join our Data Platform Engineering team! Our mission is to develop, maintain and improve Ebury's Data Platform — this role owns the Analytics Platform: the tools, frameworks, and standards that empower our Data Analysts to deliver trusted insights at scale. You will manage the full lifecycle of our BI and visualization stack, built on Sigma, together with dbt and BigQuery as the core modelling and warehousing tools, and help evolve how analysts work — bringing software engineering practices into the analytics workflow.

Responsibilities

• Own and evolve Ebury's analytics platform end-to-end, with Sigma as the core BI and visualization tool — administration, governance, versioning, and best practices

• Define and manage the SDLC for analyst workflows across dbt and BigQuery: development standards, testing, code review, CI/CD, and release processes

• Build the frameworks and guardrails that enable self-service analytics — ensuring dashboards and datasets are discoverable, documented, governed, and trustworthy

• Champion metrics consistency across the organisation, ensuring business definitions are aligned between the warehouse, semantic models, and BI layer

• Support and upskill the Data Analyst community, helping them adopt analytics-engineering practices (version control, testing, modular modelling) as their ways of working evolve

• Provide observability for analyst-facing data products: usage analytics, freshness, data quality signals, and cost/performance optimisation of BI workloads on BigQuery

• Collaborate closely with the rest of the Data Platform team — scheduler & infra, semantic layer, and AI platform — to deliver a coherent platform experience for all data domains

• Drive continuous improvement by evaluating emerging BI and analytics tooling, patterns, and best practices in the modern data stack

About you

• Self-motivation and curiosity, with a desire to learn and grow in a fast-paced environment, continuously improving both technical and business skills

• Platform engineering experience building internal platforms consumed by other teams — ideally analytics or BI platforms

• Hands-on expertise administering and scaling a modern BI tool (Sigma strongly preferred; experience with comparable tools such as Looker or Tableau also valued)

• Deep experience with dbt and BigQuery — project structuring, testing strategies, performance and cost optimisation

• Strong SQL proficiency and solid Python skills for tooling and automation

• Experience establishing SDLC practices for analytics teams: Git workflows, CI/CD, testing, and documentation standards

• Solid understanding of data governance concepts — lineage, access controls, cataloging — as they apply to the BI layer

• Strong communication and enablement skills — you enjoy teaching, documenting, and raising the bar for how analysts work

About the Team

The Code Quality team sits within the Developer Platform organization and owns the systems that keep DoorDash's codebase healthy and secure as it scales: static analysis, quality gates, test frameworks, regression infrastructure, and tooling. Our job is to make sure the signals engineers rely on before shipping — test results, coverage, performance feedback etc — are fast and trustworthy. The decisions we make about tooling and standards directly shape how confidently and quickly engineering teams at DoorDash can ship to production.

About the Role

We're looking for Software Engineers to help build and maintain the systems that validate code quality across DoorDash's engineering org, treating our tooling as a critical product for the engineers who rely on it every day: static analysis and quality gates, test frameworks and regression infrastructure. You’ll design the tooling and automation that will help derive trustworthy quality signals, integrate them into the development lifecycle, and make it easy for engineers to execute reliable, repeatable workflows. You will collaborate across the engineering org, partnering directly with the teams who use what you build to understand the accuracy, reliability and performance of their functionality. You will report into the Engineering Manager on our Code Quality team in our Developer Platform organization. You must be located in either San Francisco, CA, Sunnyvale, CA, Los Angeles, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Build and maintain quality tooling — static analysis, quality gates, coverage reporting, test frameworks, regression infrastructure — and integrate it directly into our developer workflows and CI/CD pipelines

• Define and derive quality signals - flakiness, pass rate, coverage, performance, scale readiness etc -

• Build tooling that improves everyday engineering workflows, including local development, CI/CD, debugging, and rollouts

• Explore how AI agents and tools can automate parts of building quality checks, and use real engineering usage data to measure their impact

• Partner directly with engineering, product, and QA teams across DoorDash to find their biggest bottlenecks and ship tooling that demonstrably improves them

We're excited about you because…

• Have experience building software quality infrastructure, test automation, meaningful ownership of build systems, CI/CD infrastructure, or developer productivity tooling

• You have a strong debugging track record and have shipped changes that measurably improved an engineering team's workflow

• You communicate clearly and partner effectively across functions — with engineers, product managers, and QA — to understand and solve real problems

• You're comfortable working through ambiguous, cross-team problems and taking them to a solution with minimal guidance

• You have proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

jobs.title: Senior Electrical Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

Partnering with design engineers early on in the process, you will ensure manufacturability, build the first prototype, design the build flow and fixturing, and finalize the process for transition to production. Once transitioned, you will have the opportunity to make a positive impact scaling production to meet K2’s ever-growing demand. You will implement new techniques for manufacturing complex PCBAs, harnessing, and integrated electronics systems. You'll also partner closely with mechanical teams on the electromechanical assemblies and machined components these electronics integrate into. In your first 6 months you will develop manufacturing methods and tooling for integrated avionics systems, define manufacturing flows for electronic subsystems, and collaborate with design teams to provide Design-for-Excellence (DFX) guidance across PCBs, PCBAs, machined components, and higher-level assemblies. . In your first year you will implement these advanced manufacturing techniques on flight hardware and scale the technology you develop to high-rate production.

Responsibilities

• Lead design-for-excellence reviews with design engineers across PCBs, PCBAs, machined components, and assemblies for initial design, flight hardware, and tooling

• Lead the development of innovative manufacturing systems for spacecraft electronic assemblies, including electromechanical sub-assemblies, and harnessing.

• Create custom tools and processes to support the manufacturing technologies you create, including Manufacturing Execution System (MES) software

• Demonstrate the advanced manufacturing techniques on prototypes, working with the design teams to continuously improve the manufacturability of the designs

• Develop the subassembly build flow and iterate to create an efficient production flow for the satellite and ensure that build times align with current takt times

• Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior Manufacturing Engineers, technicians, and design peers on electronics manufacturing best practices

• Partner with a team of advanced manufacturing engineers to perform R&D of novel manufacturing technologies for current and future spacecraft products

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, aerospace, or other relevant engineering discipline

• 6+ years of experience in a high volume, rapid production environment in a manufacturing, integration, and/or design engineering role

• Demonstrated track record leading product development and/or process improvements

• Strong understanding of IPC standards (e.g., IPC-A-610, IPC-A-600, J-STD-001) for PCB/PCBA workmanship and inspection

• Strong understanding of how to set up a manufacturing/production floor for first article builds and transitioning from low to high-rate manufacturing.

• Deep understanding of avionics subassembly manufacturing technologies, including PCBA assembly, wire harness manufacturing and PCBA/mechanical enclosure integration

• Strong understanding DFX guidance to design teams across PCBs, PCBAs, machined components, and mechanical assemblies

• Strong understanding of GD&T and mechanical assembly drawings, with the ability to review and provide feedback on electrical and mechanical designs

• Good understanding of conformal coating processes (selective spray, dip, or brush application) and associated inspection/rework methods for PCBAs, per standards such as IPC-CC-830 and NASA-STD-8739.1

Nice to Have

• Strong understanding and track record of tooling design for electromechanical subassemblies and electronics

• Demonstrated ability to independently develop production processes from the ground up, including driving design improvements for manufacturing

• Strong understanding of technician workflows and build tooling, with a track record of working closely with production teams to implement feedback-driven process improvements. Experience with aerospace manufacturing standards such as soldering standards, torque specifications, and quality assurance standards

• Familiarity with CAD software (NX or equivalent) and GD&T

• Strong understanding and experience working with MES, with the ability to set up the foundation for procedure creation, template generation and documentation of non-conformances

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $140,000 – $175,000 + equity in the company

• Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision/ coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license.

Equal Opportunity

K2 Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with K2 Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Restaurant Product
jobs.description:
With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

About the Job

OpenTable's Restaurant Product team builds the tools that help restaurants run smarter, more profitable businesses. We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead the vision and execution of AI/ML-powered products that directly optimize revenue for restaurants on our platform. In this role, you will define and launch 0-to-1 products, partner closely with engineering and design to iterate quickly, and align stakeholders across the company around a clear, compelling product strategy. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role for someone who thrives on solving ambiguous problems with emerging technology and translating business acumen and data into products that ship fast and deliver measurable value.

Responsibilities

• Define and drive the product vision and strategy for solutions that optimize revenue for restaurants.

• Lead the end-to-end development of 0-to-1, AI/ML-powered products, from concept through launch.

• Partner with engineering and design to rapidly prototype, test, and iterate on new product concepts.

• Use data analytics to identify revenue opportunities, prioritize the roadmap, and measure the impact of shipped features.

• Align cross-functional stakeholders and executives around product priorities and trade-offs.

• Translate business objectives into a compelling product narrative that guides teams toward shared outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years of product management experience, including leading complex, high-impact initiatives.

• Demonstrated experience building and shipping AI/ML-powered products.

• Proven track record of taking 0-to-1 products from concept to launch.

• Strong business acumen and the ability to translate data analytics into strategic product decisions.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience aligning executives and cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in the restaurant, hospitality, or marketplace industry.

• Background in revenue management, pricing, or yield-optimization products.

• Familiarity with rapid experimentation frameworks and agile/lean methodologies.

• Experience working with two-sided marketplaces.

• Advanced technical fluency in AI/ML concepts and applications.

Benefits and Perks

• Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year

• Focus on mental health and well-being:

• Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth

• Company-paid subscription to Headspace

• Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

• Paid parental leave

• Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday

• Paid volunteer time

• Focus on your career growth:

• Development Dollars

• Leadership development

• Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

• Travel Discounts

• Employee Resource Groups

• Free lunch 2 days per week

• Convenient downtown SF office location close to the Embarcadero MUNI and BART stations.

• Building amenities, such as a gym & bike parking

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

There are a variety of factors that go into determining a salary range, including but not limited to external market benchmark data, geographic location, and years of experience sought/required. The range for this United States based role is $190,000-$220,000.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus and equity grant.

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations.

jobs.title: Principal Mechanisms Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

Partnering with the Mechanisms Engineering team early on in the process, you will ensure manufacturability, build the first prototype, design the build flow and fixturing, and finalize the process for transition to production. Once transitioned, you will have the opportunity to make a positive impact scaling production to meet K2’s ever-growing demand. You will implement new techniques for manufacturing complex mechanisms – including rotational actuators, separation mechanisms, gimbals, and reaction wheel assemblies – as well as the electromechanical assemblies and machined components they integrate into. In your first 6 months you will develop manufacturing methods and tooling for these mechanisms, define manufacturing flows for mechanism subsystems, build test articles to support the Mechanisms Engineering team’s development and qualification test campaigns, and provide Design-for-Excellence (DFX) guidance across mechanisms, machined components, and higher-level assemblies. In your first year you will implement these advanced manufacturing techniques on flight hardware and scale the technology you develop to high-rate production. As a Principal on the team, you will also set manufacturing policy and standards, proactively flag risk in upcoming mechanism designs before it becomes a problem, plan ahead for the manufacturability of future programs, and build tools that make the rest of the Manufacturing Engineering team faster and more effective.

Responsibilities

• Lead design-for-excellence (DFX) reviews with the Mechanisms Engineering team, providing manufacturability, testability, and assembly guidance across mechanisms, machined components, and assemblies for initial design, flight hardware, and tooling

• Lead the development of innovative manufacturing systems for spacecraft mechanisms, including rotational actuators, separation mechanisms, gimbals, and reaction wheel assemblies

• Set manufacturing policy, standards, and best practices for the Manufacturing Engineering organization, proactively identifying and mitigating manufacturability, process, and quality risks before they surface

• Plan manufacturing strategy, tooling, and capacity investments ahead of future mechanism designs and program roadmaps

• Research and pilot new assembly methodologies and automation technologies, using data-driven analysis to optimize current production and inform manufacturing business decisions

• Create custom tools, automation, and processes — including Manufacturing Execution System (MES) software — to support the manufacturing technologies you create and streamline the work of the broader Manufacturing Engineering team

• Demonstrate the advanced manufacturing techniques on prototypes, working with the design teams to continuously improve the manufacturability of the designs

• Build test articles and support the Mechanisms Engineering team’s development and qualification test campaigns, iterating on hardware and processes as test results come in

• Develop the subassembly build flow and iterate to create an efficient production flow for the satellite and ensure that build times align with current takt times

• Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior manufacturing engineers, technicians, and design peers on mechanisms manufacturing best practices

• Partner with a team of advanced manufacturing engineers to lead R&D of novel manufacturing technologies for current and future spacecraft products

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, electrical, or other relevant engineering discipline

• 10+ years of experience in a high volume, rapid production environment in a manufacturing, integration, and/or design engineering role

• Demonstrated track record of leading product development and/or process improvement initiatives

• Strong understanding of mechanisms-specific industry standards such as NASA-STD-5017 (Design and Development Requirements for Mechanisms) and AIAA S-114 (Moving Mechanical Assemblies for Space and Launch Vehicles), as well as familiarity with the environmental qualification standards (SMC-S-016, GSFC-STD-7000) the Mechanisms Engineering team designs against

• Strong understanding of how to set up a manufacturing/production floor for first article builds and transitioning from low to high-rate manufacturing

• Deep understanding of mechanisms subassembly manufacturing technologies, including rotational actuators, separation mechanisms, gimbals, and reaction wheel assemblies

• Strong understanding of design-for-excellence (DFX) principles, with the ability to guide design teams across mechanisms, machined components, and mechanical assemblies

• Strong understanding of GD&T (geometric dimensioning and tolerancing) and mechanical assembly drawings, with the ability to review and provide feedback on electrical and mechanical designs

• Demonstrated ability to set manufacturing policy and proactively identify and mitigate manufacturing risk across programs, and to influence cross-functional teams to drive design changes for manufacturability

• Experience developing or deploying tools, automation, or software that scale the efficiency of a manufacturing engineering team

Nice to Have

• Familiarity with precision bearing standards (e.g., ABMA) and bearing preload techniques and measurement, as used in rotational actuators, gimbals, and reaction wheel assemblies

• Experience designing tooling for mechanisms and electromechanical subassemblies

• Some experience with wire harness manufacturing and integration

• Demonstrated experience developing production processes from the ground up, including driving design improvements for manufacturing

• Experience working closely with technicians and build tooling

• Experience with aerospace manufacturing standards such as lubrication practices, torque specifications, and quality assurance standards

• Familiarity with CAD software (NX or equivalent)

• Familiarity with data analytics tools (e.g., Python, SQL) or automation platforms used to process manufacturing data and drive business decisions

• Experience working with MES to set up the foundation for procedure creation and documenting non-conformances

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $175,000 – $200,000 + equity in the company

• Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision/ coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

jobs.title: Foundation Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT ALU

At the African Leadership University (ALU), we're more than just an institution—we're a catalyst for transformation. Our mission is to develop a new generation of ethical and entrepreneurial leaders who will shape Africa's future. Through our innovative curriculum, focus on experiential learning, and vibrant pan-African community, we empower students to become changemakers, problem-solvers, and innovators. At ALU, we're not just teaching; we're nurturing the leaders who will drive Africa's progress and prosperity in the 21st century

We are dedicated to fostering an open yet secure environment, balancing the safety of students, staff, and visitors with respect for individual rights, and safeguarding responsibilities.

HOW WE WORK

The ALU Team works in starkly different ways to traditional academic bureaucracies. We approach education from first principles, empower individuals to design, test, and implement creative new ideas, and work closely together to craft transformative learning experiences. We are deeply passionate about our students and excited by the challenge of building something entirely new.

The African Leadership University is committed to ensuring the safety and Well-being of all students under our care. As part of this commitment , we have a comprehensive safeguarding policy in place , which outlines our Zero-tolerance approach to any violation of safeguarding.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Foundation Lead supports the Foundation Manager in ensuring the coherent design, quality and delivery of the Foundation and Leadership Core learning experience. The
postholder provides academic and operational leadership across entrepreneurship, Responsible Enterprise, project-related learning and other foundational courses, while
managing and supporting faculty to deliver consistent, rigorous and learner-centred experiences. The role connects curriculum, people and programme operations. It ensures that course content remains relevant, assessments are well designed and moderated, Canvas course environments are ready, faculty are equipped to facilitate effectively, and students receive timely academic support. The Foundation Lead also contributes to continuous improvement, cross-programme alignment and the development of scalable experiential learning.

Responsibilities

Academic Leadership and Curriculum Stewardship

• Lead the planning, coordination, delivery and continuous improvement of assigned Foundation and Leadership Core courses, with particular responsibility for entrepreneurship, Responsible Enterprise and project-related learning.

• Review and refine curricula, learning outcomes, session guides, Canvas materials, assessments and rubrics to ensure academic coherence, appropriate challenge and alignment with the institution's learning model.

• Ensure that entrepreneurship learning develops opportunity recognition, customer and stakeholder understanding, experimentation, business modelling, resourcefulness and ethical value creation.

• Ensure that Responsible Enterprise learning integrates ethics, sustainability, stakeholder responsibility, governance and the social and environmental consequences of enterprise decisions.

• Strengthen project-based learning by establishing clear project briefs, milestones, supervision processes, feedback cycles, presentation standards and authentic assessment practices.

• Support the integration of critical thinking, managing complex tasks, self-directed learning, reflective practice, collaboration and communication across the Foundation experience.

• Maintain definitive course documentation for programme handbooks, quality assurance reviews, accreditation processes and institutional reporting.

People Management and Team Support

• Manage, coach and support a team of faculty, facilitators and associate faculty, setting clear expectations for preparation, delivery, assessment, learner support and professional conduct.

• Lead faculty onboarding, induction and re-induction, ensuring that team members understand course intent, learning outcomes, facilitation approaches, assessment requirements and operational processes.

• Hold regular one-to-one and team check-ins; provide timely feedback; agree development goals; and contribute to probation, performance review and other people-management processes.

• Observe teaching and facilitation, review course evidence and learner feedback, and provide practical coaching that strengthens inclusive, experiential and discussion-based pedagogy.

• Build a collaborative team culture in which faculty share resources and challenges, calibrate academic judgment, solve delivery issues collectively and learn from one another.

• Plan faculty allocation and workload with the Foundation Manager, identify capacity or performance risks early, and coordinate appropriate support or escalation.

• Promote staff wellbeing and sustainable working practices while maintaining accountability for agreed standards, timelines and learner outcomes.

Delivery, Assessment and Learner Support

• Coordinate trimester readiness, including course-shell verification, publication of learning materials, faculty allocation, delivery schedules, assessment calendars and learner communications.

• Monitor the quality and consistency of in-person, blended and online delivery, and address gaps in preparation, facilitation, accessibility or learner engagement.

• Lead assessment briefing, moderation, grading calibration and results review processes, ensuring fairness, transparency, academic integrity and timely feedback.

• Use attendance, participation, assessment and student-feedback data to identify learners or cohorts requiring support and coordinate appropriate academic interventions with relevant teams.

• Guide undergraduate projects and applied learning activities, helping students translate ideas into disciplined inquiry, responsible action and demonstrable outputs.

• Support academic orientation, programme induction and learning-transition activities for new and continuing students.

Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement

• Conduct regular course audits and contribute to annual and periodic programme reviews, using evidence from learner outcomes, faculty reflections, student evaluations and stakeholder feedback.

• Implement approved modifications to learning materials, assessments and delivery approaches in response to internal and external quality assurance findings.

• Support consistent academic standards across cohorts, programmes and campuses through shared templates, moderation, documentation and communities of practice.

• Prepare concise reports and recommendations for the Foundation Manager on delivery performance, learner progress, faculty support needs, risks and improvement priorities.

• Ensure that course design and delivery comply with institutional policies on assessment, attendance, accessibility, safeguarding, data protection, academic integrity and the responsible use of AI.

Partnerships, Applied Learning and Institutional Contribution

• Develop and maintain relationships with entrepreneurs, enterprises, community organisations and other partners that can enrich projects, cases, guest sessions, field experiences and learner feedback.

• Work with the Foundation Manager to assess partnership opportunities, draft concept notes and translate relevant external engagement into well-scaffolded learning experiences.

• Contribute to student-staff consultative forums, faculty working groups, committees and other institutional service activities as requested.

• Undertake other reasonable duties assigned by the Foundation Manager in support of successful Foundation and Leadership Core delivery.

Key Working Relationships

• Internal: Foundation Manager; Foundation and Leadership Core faculty; programme managers and leads; Registrar and academic operations; quality assurance; student success; Centre for Applied Learning and Innovation (CALI), Centre for Entrepreneurship (C4E) learning design and technology teams.

• External: entrepreneurs, responsible businesses, community partners, guest practitioners, project clients and learning-content partners.

Requirements

Essential

• A master's degree in entrepreneurship, business, education, sustainability, project management, leadership or another field relevant to the role.

• At least three years of relevant professional experience, including a minimum of two years in higher education, training, learning design or academic programme delivery.

• Demonstrable subject knowledge and practical experience in at least two of the following: entrepreneurship, Responsible Enterprise, sustainability, business ethics, project-based learning or project management.

• Experience designing and delivering experiential, applied or project-based learning for undergraduate learners or adult professionals.

• Experience guiding student projects, assessing complex outputs and providing developmental feedback.

• Experience managing, supervising or coaching faculty or multidisciplinary delivery teams, including setting expectations and supporting performance and development.

• Strong curriculum and assessment design capability, with an understanding of constructive alignment, rubric design, moderation and quality assurance.

• Ability to interpret academic and engagement data, identify risks and determine appropriate learner or faculty support interventions.

• Excellent written and spoken English, facilitation, presentation, interpersonal and stakeholder-management skills.

• Strong planning, judgement and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver reliably in a fast-moving environment.

• Commitment to inclusive, learner-centred education, ethical leadership and high standards of professional practice.

• Confidence working with digital learning platforms such as Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard or Google Classroom, as well as collaborative productivity tools.

Desirable

• Experience in programme management or academic leadership within a higher education institution.
